method: Actually inspected all three source-left/C-right contact sheets and three C native frames with view_image at original detail. No continuous video playback was performed.

shirt_color.assessment: The man's shirt is visibly red at all nine inspected contact-sheet points and all three inspected native C frames.
shirt_color.scope: Sampled-frame color success only; this does not establish success of the complete preserve-only editing instruction.

woman_clothing.assessment: The woman's visible garment remains white in the inspected samples, without an obvious red recoloring of it.
woman_clothing.qualification: The substantially changed viewing arrangement reveals different garment surfaces and folds. Exact fabric, shape and detail preservation is not established.

coarse_actions_and_order.source_in_contact_sheets: The source starts face-to-face with the man holding the woman's head, proceeds through approach and a kiss around frame 30, then separation around frame 45 and a chest embrace from around frame 60 onward; the woman's face is outward/toward the camera late in the source.
coarse_actions_and_order.C_in_contact_sheets: C already starts in a kiss with the man's arm around the woman's waist. The early and middle samples remain predominantly face-to-face/kissing, and the late samples show the couple facing each other and smiling with their faces close together. Native frame 60 is still a kiss, and native frame 123 is face-to-face smiling rather than the source's late chest-embrace pose.
coarse_actions_and_order.assessment: The observed C sequence does not preserve the source's approach-to-kiss-to-chest-embrace progression. This is a substantive action-content/order/timing mismatch, not merely uncertainty about exact frame alignment.
coarse_actions_and_order.not_a_freeze: Head poses, smiles, relative posture and composition change across the C samples; the inspected output should not be described as a static or frozen video.

people_and_viewing_arrangement.assessment: In the source contact images the woman is on the left and the man on the right; in C the man is on the left and the woman on the right, with different visible sides of their faces/bodies and different hand placement. The couple remains broadly recognizable as a man and brown-haired woman, but exact identity preservation is not established from these changed views.
people_and_viewing_arrangement.causal_limit: The images establish a changed viewing arrangement; they do not establish whether its cause is camera movement, actor rotation or another generative change.

background_lighting_and_framing.assessment: C introduces a conspicuous large dark tree and a dark distant tree line with a different landscape arrangement from the source's open pale sky/grass and smaller distant tree clumps. The couple's crop, visible head/body surfaces and placement differ substantially. C also appears darker and more contrasty in the inspected comparisons.
background_lighting_and_framing.instruction_compliance: The requested preservation of viewpoint/framing/background/lighting is visibly not satisfied at the sampled points.

native_frame_artifacts.assessment: Native C frames 0, 60 and 123 show coherent full images without an observed black screen or whole-frame collapse. The main concrete defects for this task are the altered interaction, viewing arrangement, composition and background, rather than an established gross rendering collapse.
native_frame_artifacts.qualification: No claim is made that hands, faces, cloth details or temporal transitions are artifact-free; only three native output frames were inspected.

conclusion.limited_task_assessment: The red-shirt color objective is visible in the inspected C frames, and the woman's garment remains white, but C fails the broader instruction to change only the shirt color while retaining the original action progression and scene composition.

limitations: This review inspected nine contact-sheet timestamps and three native C frames, not every output frame and not continuous video playback.
Audio was not played or evaluated.
Native source images were not opened separately; source comparisons use the left-hand source panels of the three contact sheets.
A and B images/videos were not reopened in this review, so this record does not establish a full cross-case equal-quality ranking.
Exact event timing, motion smoothness, flicker, lip behavior and small intermittent defects cannot be established from these sparse stills.

This review does not independently validate video extraction, full-video SHA, frame count, PTS, model execution or source/prompt provenance; the six actually viewed image files are bound by SHA256 above.
Latency numbers were not used to judge image quality. Faster execution cannot compensate for the observed preserve-only instruction failures.
The visual mismatch alone does not prove its implementation or algorithmic cause.
